It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. div.head: ECf 36.4
div.ab: Quodsi interfectori defecerint iudices et testes, et diracionatum fuerit, quod iniuste sit interfectus, interfector dabit uadimonium iusticie episcopi et fideiussores.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 667 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

seg.hi: Umstand des Gerichts, welches jenen hingerichtet hatte (wohl nicht Eideshelfer oder Zeugen, die gegen ihn ausgesagt hatten)

note.seg: the bystanders of the court which had executed him (probably not oath-helpers or witnesses who had testified against him)
vgl. 2, 9. 8, 2. Der weltliche Richter hat bereits (36, 2) Pfand empfangen
cf. 2, 9. 8, 2. The secular judge has already (36, 2) received a pledge
i. sit S; lacking in Hr

div.ab: But if the slayer lacks judges and witnesses, and it is deraigned that he was killed unjustly, the slayer shall give a gage to the bishop's justice, and sureties.

note.seg: Vgl. Geistliches Gericht 3. 27c; Bischof 9e. — Des Retr.'s letzte drei Worte verwirren die Parteirollen — disr. f. q. iniuste23 [richtig] Rs
